independent_confirmation_of_the_reported.hq_claim: the comment 'PyList_AsTuple CONSUMES the ordered reference' is false; PyList_AsTuple returns a new tuple reference and does NOT steal the input list, so `ordered` leaks on both the success and failure paths
independent_confirmation_of_the_reported.how_confirmed: not from memory or from a comment, but empirically on this governed CPython 3.11.3 by calling the C API through ctypes with explicit argtypes and measuring the input list's refcount delta
independent_confirmation_of_the_reported.header: include/python3.11/listobject.h:41 declares PyAPI_FUNC(PyObject *) PyList_AsTuple(PyObject *); with no steal annotation
independent_confirmation_of_the_reported.correct_pattern_used_elsewhere_in_this_f: admit_relation already did it correctly: tup = PyList_AsTuple(srcs); Py_DECREF(srcs); srcs = tup;
independent_confirmation_of_the_reported.note_on_my_own_prior_work: this false comment was introduced by ME in HQ247. I asserted a steal semantic that the API does not have, and asserted it without verifying. The reproduction script for this commission exists so the next reviewer does not have to trust my word for it.

self_inflicted_defect_removed.history: in HQ245 I added an unconditional Py_INCREF to the result of trusted canonicalize, believing the trusted seam could return its input unchanged and that the result was therefore not owned. That belief was wrong: PyObject_CallFunctionObjArgs already returns a NEW owned reference.
self_inflicted_defect_removed.consequence: that INCREF leaked one reference per trusted_canon call forever
self_inflicted_defect_removed.why_it_was_invisible: on the positive decide path the canonicalised values are interned strings, so an extra reference cost ZERO pymalloc blocks and was invisible; on the negative path the freshly allocated operation_scope/effective_scope dicts cost real blocks, which is why only the negative path showed the symptom
self_inflicted_defect_removed.repair: the extra INCREF is removed; the call's own returned reference is the ownership
self_inflicted_defect_removed.verification: all 397 existing tests still pass with it removed, so it was never load-bearing -- the HQ245 EXC_BAD_ACCESS was caused by the separate borrowed-argument over-DECREF (MEM-002), not by this
